s: What does overlay analysis in GIS refer to?
o: Converting raster data into vector data
Creating a buffer zone around a feature
Combining different data layers for analysis
x: Overlay analysis combines multiple thematic layers to derive and analyse relationships between them.

s: In a GIS, QGIS is an example of which of the following?
x: QGIS is GIS software; GIS hardware means the computer, digitizer, scanner, GPS receiver and plotter.

s: In a GIS work station, what is the function of a digitizer?
o: It converts analog maps and data into digital format
It prints the final maps on paper
It stores satellite images on a server
It receives signals from GPS satellites
x: A digitizer is a tablet or table on which analog data such as paper maps are converted into digital form.

s: Which of the following is NOT a hardware component of GIS?
x: QGIS is free, open-source GIS software; scanner, plotter and GPS receiver are hardware.

s: In a GIS, in what form is each theme of data, such as roads or rivers, stored?
x: In GIS each theme is stored as a separate layer; overlay analysis combines these layers.

s: Which use of GIS gives emergency teams real-time layers for flood alerts and shoreline mapping during disasters?
x: GIS gives situational awareness through real-time layers for disaster response, flood alerts and shoreline mapping.

s: Which satellite system supports flood mapping even through cloud cover?
x: RISAT's SAR can map floods through clouds; INSAT-3DS tracks cyclones, Oceansat gives ocean-state data and Cartosat maps damage.

s: What does Bhuvan mainly provide by combining RISAT/SAR imagery and INSAT-3DS cyclone-track data?
x: Bhuvan combines RISAT/SAR flood imagery and INSAT-3DS cyclone-track information to support flood-inundation mapping and cyclone warnings.

s: What is the abbreviation of the National Database for Emergency Management?
x: NDEM is the National Database for Emergency Management. NADAMS is the drought system and DMSP ISRO's programme.

s: In the INSAT Disaster Warning System, how do warnings from the Cyclone Warning Centre, Chennai travel?
x: The chain is Cyclone Warning Centre, Chennai, then C-band uplink, then S-band downlink to coastal disaster-warning receivers.

s: For what does the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) use GIS?
o: Planning, decision support and developing guidelines
x: NDMA uses GIS for planning, decision support and drafting guidelines.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about fire-hotspot monitoring?
o: Hotspot data are passed to the India Meteorological Department, which runs the forest-fire alert system
Thermal-infrared sensors such as MODIS and VIIRS detect fire hotspots
MODIS flies on NASA's Terra and Aqua satellites
Hotspot data are received at NRSC's Shadnagar earth station
x: The hotspot data go to the Forest Survey of India alert system, not to IMD.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about satellite support during disasters in India?
o: The Decision Support Centre is located at NRSC, Hyderabad
States can use satellite data during disasters without requesting it from NRSC
The National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM) is located at NRSC, Hyderabad
The Decision Support Centre acts as a single window for satellite inputs during disasters
x: States must request satellite data from NRSC; the other statements are correct.

s: From which month did ISRO take the lead role in the International Charter Space and Major Disasters for six months?
x: ISRO assumed the lead role in the International Charter Space and Major Disasters for six months from April 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ISRO's Disaster Management Support Programme?
o: It uses INSAT and IRS satellite systems
It is limited to cyclone warnings alone
It provides communication support during disasters
x: The programme gives imaging and communication support for floods, cyclones, droughts and other disasters, so it is not limited to cyclones.

s: Which pair of thermal-infrared sensors is used to detect forest-fire hotspots?
x: Fire hotspots come from MODIS (NASA Terra/Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP).

s: Where does the Decision Support Centre, a single window for satellite inputs during disasters, function?
x: The Decision Support Centre is at NRSC, and States must request data from NRSC.

s:
Consider the following statements about disaster monitoring from space:
1. Post-earthquake ground deformation can be monitored from space.
2. Earthquakes can be predicted using satellite remote sensing.
3. Tsunami inundation can be mapped from space.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Ground deformation after a quake and tsunami inundation can be monitored; earthquake prediction cannot.

s: Satellite fire-hotspot alerts received at Shadnagar feed the alert system of which organisation?
x: Fire-hotspot data go to the Forest Survey of India alert system, not IMD.

s: Which of the following cannot be monitored using satellite remote sensing?
x: Satellites can monitor cyclones, forest fires and landslides, but not a human-health event such as a heart attack.

s: For which hazard does NRSC identify the Ganga-Brahmaputra basin as the most prone area in India?
x: NRSC's flood disaster management study names the Ganga-Brahmaputra basin as the most flood-prone area in India.

s: Which satellite is mainly used for damage mapping after disasters?
x: Cartosat gives high-resolution images for damage mapping; INSAT-3DS tracks cyclones.

s: Which one of the following agencies functions as the nodal agency for receiving, processing and supplying satellite data, while also operating Bhuvan and providing disaster-support services to States?
x: The National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Hyderabad, receives, processes and supplies satellite data, runs Bhuvan and supports States in disaster management.

s: Where is the North Eastern Space Applications Centre (NESAC) located?
x: NESAC is at Umiam (Shillong), Meghalaya, a joint body of the Department of Space and the North Eastern Council.

s: Which institution is responsible for training and education in remote sensing and GIS?
x: IIRS, Dehradun handles training and education in remote sensing and GIS; NESAC serves the North-East and SAC builds sensors.

s: How many Regional Remote Sensing Centres (RRSCs) function under NRSC?
x: Five RRSCs, at Bengaluru, Jodhpur, Kharagpur, Nagpur and Delhi, work under NRSC on regional projects for States.

s: Where is NRSC's satellite earth station, which also receives fire-hotspot data, located?
x: NRSC's earth station is at Shadnagar, where MODIS and VIIRS fire-hotspot data are received.

s: Which ISRO centre runs the MOSDAC and VEDAS portals?
x: The Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad runs MOSDAC, VEDAS and Nabhmitra, and builds sensors and payloads.

s: Which of the following is NOT the location of a Regional Remote Sensing Centre (RRSC) of NRSC?
x: The 5 RRSCs are at Bengaluru, Jodhpur, Kharagpur, Nagpur and Delhi; NRSC itself is at Hyderabad.

s: Which portal provides meteorological and oceanographic satellite data?
x: MOSDAC (SAC) provides meteorological and oceanographic satellite data; Bhoonidhi (NRSC) is an EO data archive and VEDAS visualises EO data.

s: Which of the following portal–use pairs is wrongly matched?
o: PM Gati Shakti – National Master Plan GIS platform
SVAMITVA – Drone mapping and property cards
Bhuvan Panchayat – Geospatial support for Gram Panchayat development planning
Yuktdhara – National Master Plan GIS platform
x: Yuktdhara is for planning and monitoring MGNREGA assets; the National Master Plan GIS platform is PM Gati Shakti.

s: Which organisation developed the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan GIS platform?
x: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan GIS platform was built by BISAG-N.

s: In which year was ISRO's geoportal Bhuvan, developed by NRSC, Hyderabad, launched?
x: Bhuvan was launched in 2009 by NRSC; 2012 is the year MNCFC was set up.

s: In partnership with which organisation does SVAMITVA map rural properties by drone?
x: SVAMITVA uses drone mapping of rural properties with the Survey of India to issue property cards.

s: Which NRSC portal archives Earth-observation data since 1988 for search and download?
x: Bhoonidhi is NRSC's EO data archive; VEDAS and MOSDAC belong to SAC and Srishti monitors watersheds.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Bhuvan Panchayat serves gram panchayat planning; Srishti is for watersheds, Yuktdhara for MGNREGA assets and MOSDAC for disaster alerts.

s: Which of the following satellites is an example of active (radar) remote sensing?
x: Active systems transmit their own signal, as RISAT's radar does; Resourcesat and Oceansat illustrate passive sensing of naturally available radiation.

s: SAR (microwave) remote sensing is especially useful for flood mapping because it can:
o: Observe through cloud cover and in darkness
Measure thermal emission from water bodies
Record images only in visible light
Operate only in daylight under clear skies
x: Microwave/SAR systems can observe through cloud cover and in darkness, making them useful for flood mapping in cloudy conditions.

s: InSAR detects ground deformation by comparing which property of two or more radar images of the same area?
x: Interferometric SAR compares the phase of two or more radar images of the same area to detect ground deformation.

s: Which type of sensor is best suited for measuring soil moisture from space?
x: Microwave and SAR sensors are particularly suitable for soil-moisture measurement; NISAR uses L-band and S-band radar for this.

s: Which observations does NISAR use to detect centimetre-scale ground movement for studying land subsidence, earthquakes and glaciers?
x: NISAR uses radar observations, which let it detect centimetre-scale ground movement.

s: Remote sensing is used to assess which of the following natural-resource features?
o: Surface and groundwater prospects, snow and glaciers, wetlands, and mineral and hydrocarbon zones
x: All of these are listed as measurable by remote sensing, along with land cover, vegetation, soil and crop yield.

s: Oceansat and Resourcesat are examples of which of the following?
x: They use natural radiation (sunlight), so they are passive; RISAT radar, which sends its own signal, is active.

s: Which of the following can be estimated using satellite remote sensing?
o: Soil nutrient levels by laboratory chemical testing
Spread of a disease among humans
x: Remote sensing can estimate crop yield (YES-TECH); chemical soil testing, disease spread and earthquake prediction are not remote-sensing tasks.

s: Which two radar bands does NISAR use?
x: NISAR carries L-band and S-band radar to measure centimetre-scale ground movement.

s: How is the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) computed?
x: NDVI = (NIR − Red) / (NIR + Red); it works because healthy vegetation reflects strongly in the near-infrared band.

s: Which index is most widely used for the operational assessment of drought?
x: NDVI is the most widely used spectral vegetation index for operational drought assessment.

s: Which of the following does the NH Green Cover Index 2025-26, India's first satellite-based green-cover assessment of its kind, cover?
x: The NH Green Cover Index is India's first satellite-based green-cover assessment of highways and uses chlorophyll detection.

s: From which data is the Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), used in drought declaration, derived?
x: VCI is derived from vegetation-related NDVI data and is used in drought declaration.

s: What is the full form of NDVI?
x: NDVI is the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index, computed as (NIR - Red)/(NIR + Red).

s: In which part of the spectrum does healthy vegetation reflect most strongly, which is used in NDVI?
x: Healthy vegetation reflects strongly in near-infrared; NDVI = (NIR - Red)/(NIR + Red).

s:
Consider the following statements about NDVI:
1. Its value ranges from -1 to +1.
2. It is the most widely used index for operational drought assessment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NDVI ranges from -1 to +1 and is the most widely used index for operational drought assessment.

s: What does the National Carbon Project of the ISRO-Geosphere Biosphere Programme assess?
o: Carbon pools, fluxes and net carbon balance of India's terrestrial biosphere
Ocean carbon uptake in the Indian Ocean
Carbon credits traded by Indian industries
x: Its goal is to assess the carbon pools, fluxes and net carbon balance of India's terrestrial biosphere.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Carbon Project:
1. It covers vegetation carbon pools.
2. It covers soil carbon pools.
3. It is limited to the marine biosphere.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Its components are vegetation carbon pools, soil carbon pools and soil-vegetation fluxes; it studies the terrestrial, not marine, biosphere.

s: On which satellite-derived information are Potential Fishing Zone advisories mainly prepared?
x: PFZ advisories identify fish-rich areas using satellite observations of chlorophyll and sea-surface temperature.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: CHAMAN — horticulture area and condition mapping
FASAL — pre-harvest crop acreage and production forecasts
GEMINI — mapping soil resources from satellite data
x: GEMINI sends PFZ, Ocean State Forecast and disaster alerts to fishermen. Soil-resource mapping from satellite data is associated with the Soil and Land Use Survey of India.

s: Which institution issues Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) advisories, now using EOS-06 (Oceansat-3) data?
x: INCOIS, Hyderabad issues PFZ advisories using EOS-06 (Oceansat-3) data; it also issues the Ocean State Forecast.

s: Who developed the Nabhmitra safety service for fishermen?
x: Nabhmitra comes from ISRO's SAC, Ahmedabad and gives two-way messaging via GSAT; INCOIS with AAI developed GEMINI.

s: What is Nabhmitra, tested at Neendakara in Kerala in August 2023?
o: a satellite-based safety device for fishermen
x: Nabhmitra is a satellite-based fishermen safety device developed by ISRO’s Space Applications Centre, Ahmedabad, and tested at Neendakara in August 2023.

s: About what does the satellite-based coastal-fishermen alert service run from the RTGS hub at Vijayawada warn?
o: Cyclones, high waves and fish shoals
x: The RTGS hub at Vijayawada provides satellite-based alerts to coastal fishermen about cyclones, high waves and fish shoals.

s: Who developed the GEMINI device, which gives PFZ, ocean-state and disaster alerts at sea?
x: GEMINI was developed by INCOIS with the Airports Authority of India and uses GAGAN; Nabhmitra is SAC's device.

s: What does the second-generation Distress Alert Transmitter (DAT-SG) send back to fishermen?
o: An acknowledgement of the distress alert
x: DAT-SG has a NavIC module and sends an acknowledgement back to fishermen.

s: Which institution issues the Ocean State Forecast for India's seas?
x: INCOIS, Hyderabad issues the Ocean State Forecast as well as Potential Fishing Zone advisories.

s: Which satellite system does the GEMINI device use to send alerts to fishermen at sea?
x: GEMINI, developed by INCOIS with AAI, uses GAGAN to send PFZ, ocean-state and disaster alerts.

s: Who developed the lightning-alert app Damini?
x: Damini is from IITM Pune (MoES); Mausam is IMD's weather app.

s: In which city was Andhra Pradesh's City Flood Alert system first implemented?
x: It was first implemented in Vijayawada, using satellite DEMs and Budameru flood data.

s: The MoU signed on 15 April 2026 between APSDMA and NRSC primarily seeks to address which problem in rural Andhra Pradesh?
x: The APSDMA-NRSC MoU aims to prevent lightning deaths in rural Andhra Pradesh.

s: Who developed the Mausam weather app?
x: Mausam is the weather app of the India Meteorological Department (IMD); Damini is IITM's lightning app.

s: Which institution worked with RTGS and APSDMA on Andhra Pradesh's AI-based City Flood Alert system?
x: City Flood Alert (AP) was built by RTGS, APSDMA and IIT Gandhinagar, first in Vijayawada.

s: Which vehicles does the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicle Tracking System (APMVTS) mainly track with AIS-140 devices?
x: APMVTS fitted 50,000 mineral vehicles with AIS-140 tracking devices.

s: APMVTS in Andhra Pradesh tracks about how many mineral vehicles with AIS-140 devices?
x: APMVTS fits AIS-140 devices on about 50,000 mineral vehicles.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in relation to APSAC activities?
o: VCI — Agricultural drought assessment at mandal level
YES-TECH — Yield estimation in Nandyal and Kakinada
x: APSSDI standardises GIS layers and supports spatial mapping; the satellite-based lightning alert application is not its stated function. APSAC uses VCI, YES-TECH and SVAMITVA for the functions listed in the other pairs.

s: The Andhra Pradesh State Spatial Data Infrastructure (APSSDI) has standardised how many GIS layers to ISO standards?
x: APSSDI has standardised 74 GIS layers to ISO standards and is registered with the National Data Registry.

s: How many drought mandals did Andhra Pradesh declare in 2024-25 using mandal-level VCI?
x: AP declared 103 drought mandals in 7 districts, of which 80 were severe.

s: The PM Gati Shakti platform in Andhra Pradesh has how many GIS layers?
x: Gati Shakti AP has 271 GIS layers across 27 departments; 74 is the APSSDI figure.

s: About how long is the Andhra Pradesh coastline covered by APSAC's shoreline mapping?
x: The 1,053 km coast is 26% eroded, 54% accreting and 20% stable.

s: YES-TECH yield pilots in Andhra Pradesh were run in which districts?
x: APSAC ran YES-TECH pilots in Nandyal and Kakinada.

s: What are ISRO's single-window centres for tele-education, telemedicine, weather and land/water advisories called?
x: ISRO's Village Resource Centres are single-window centres for these services.

s: Tele-education, telemedicine and Village Resource Centres in India have been enabled by which satellite systems?
x: INSAT and GSAT satellite communication systems have enabled tele-education, telemedicine and Village Resource Centres.

s: Swayam Prabha provides how many free DTH channels through GSAT-15?
x: Swayam Prabha provides 40 free DTH channels through GSAT-15.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about satellite-based timing in India?
o: Banks use it to time-stamp transactions
Power grids use it to synchronise their phase
NavIC is now India's reference for Indian Standard Time
The government wants NavIC to serve Indian Standard Time
x: GPS is the current reference; the government only wants NavIC to serve Indian Standard Time.

s: On which satellite are Swayam Prabha's educational DTH channels carried?
x: Swayam Prabha's DTH channels are on GSAT-15.

s: Why did NVS-02 attract attention in March 2026?
x: NVS-02 was stranded in the wrong orbit, limiting its intended use in the NavIC system.

s: On which satellites does GAGAN, the ISRO-AAI system, have payloads?
x: GAGAN payloads are carried on GSAT-8, GSAT-10 and GSAT-15.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about satellite-based services in India?
o: Village Resource Centres are run by IMD
Swayam Prabha offers 40 free DTH channels
ISRO Telemedicine Network links rural clinics to specialists
x: Village Resource Centres are ISRO's single-window centres, not IMD's.

s: The atomic clock of which NavIC satellite failed in March 2026, leaving only three PNT-capable satellites?
x: On 13 March 2026 the IRNSS-1F clock failed, leaving only 3 PNT-capable NavIC satellites.

s: For what are Resourcesat-series data mainly used?
o: Crop acreage assessment, watershed management and precision farming
x: Resourcesat data support crop acreage assessment, watershed management and precision farming.

s: In which year was the Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre (MNCFC), which makes ISRO's crop-forecasting methods operational, set up?
x: MNCFC was set up in 2012.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: FASAL – Satellite-based crop yield estimation for PMFBY
CHAMAN – Horticulture area and production assessment
NADAMS – Pre-harvest crop acreage and production forecasts
x: CHAMAN covers horticulture. FASAL gives pre-harvest forecasts, YES-TECH estimates yield for PMFBY and NADAMS monitors agricultural drought.

s: For what is FASAL mainly used?
o: Pre-harvest crop acreage and production forecasts
x: FASAL gives pre-harvest crop acreage and production forecasts; CHAMAN is horticulture, YES-TECH yield and NADAMS drought.

s: What does the CHAMAN programme use space technology to assess?
x: CHAMAN covers horticulture area and production; jute is under JCIS and drought under NADAMS.

s: Which programme monitors agricultural drought using satellite data?
x: NADAMS monitors agricultural drought; FASAL forecasts crops, CHAMAN covers horticulture and YES-TECH yield.

s: What does YES-TECH provide to support the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana?
x: YES-TECH estimates crop yield (such as rice) for crop insurance under PMFBY.

s: What is the full form of FASAL?
o: Forecasting Agricultural output using Space, Agro-meteorology and Land-based observations
Farm Assessment using Satellites and Land records
Forecasting Agricultural Seasons and Land use
Field Area Survey for Agricultural Lands
x: FASAL stands for Forecasting Agricultural output using Space, Agro-meteorology and Land-based observations; it gives pre-harvest forecasts.

s: Which organisation maps the soil resources of India?
o: Soil and Land Use Survey of India (SLUSI)
x: SLUSI (Soil and Land Use Survey of India) maps soil resources.

s: What wheat production for rabi 2024-25 did NRSC's CROP framework estimate using satellite data?
x: Using EOS-04, EOS-06 and Resourcesat-2A, the CROP framework estimated rabi 2024-25 wheat at 122.724 million tonnes.

s: Which organisations jointly developed Meghdoot, the app that gives agro-meteorological advisories to farmers?
x: Meghdoot gives agro-met advisories and is a joint app of IMD and ICAR.

s: What is the principal aim of Project NETRA?
o: Track only military aircraft in Indian airspace
Safeguard Indian space assets from debris and collisions
Provide satellite television services to rural areas
Develop reusable launch vehicles for lunar missions
x: Project NETRA aims to provide indigenous space situational awareness and safeguard Indian space assets from debris and collisions.

s: In which field does Bengaluru-based start-up Digantara mainly work?
o: Space situational awareness and debris tracking
x: Digantara is a space-situational-awareness start-up building space-surveillance satellites and generating debris-tracking data.

s: Which organisation runs Project NETRA, which gives 24–72 hours' warning of close approaches in space?
x: NETRA is an ISRO project to safeguard Indian space assets; IS4OM compiles the annual ISSAR.

s: How many collision avoidance manoeuvres (CAMs) did India record in 2025?
x: 18 CAMs were recorded in 2025, continuing regular CAMs for Cartosat, Resourcesat and GSAT.

s: Which ISRO system tracks debris and compiles the annual ISSAR?
x: IS4OM compiles ISSAR; NETRA is the tracking network.

s: Which Indian satellite avoided a defunct US satellite in 2019?
x: RISAT-2B made a manoeuvre in 2019 to avoid a defunct US satellite.

s: Which of the following is a private space situational awareness start-up based in Bengaluru?
x: Digantara is a private Bengaluru start-up working on space surveillance and debris tracking; IS4OM and NETRA are ISRO's.

s: What is the full form of NETRA in ISRO's Project NETRA?
o: Network for Space Object Tracking and Analysis
National Electronic Tracking and Ranging Array
Network for Earth Tracking and Remote Assessment
National Early-warning Tracking and Response Agency
x: Project NETRA is ISRO's Network for Space Object Tracking and Analysis, which safeguards Indian space assets.

s: What is the full form of IS4OM?
o: ISRO System for Safe and Sustainable Space Operations Management
Indian Space Station for Orbital Monitoring
ISRO Space Surveillance and Satellite Safety Operations Module
Integrated System for Space Object Observation and Monitoring
x: IS4OM = ISRO System for Safe and Sustainable Space Operations Management; it compiles the annual ISSAR.

s: In which year was ISRO's IS4OM facility for space situational awareness dedicated to the nation?
x: IS4OM was dedicated to the nation by Dr Jitendra Singh in 2022.

s: Which of the following defines space debris?
o: Operational satellites that have drifted from their assigned orbit
All non-functional man-made objects, including fragments, in orbit or re-entering
Natural meteoroids passing through Earth orbit
Fragments created only by anti-satellite tests
x: Space debris consists of non-functional man-made objects, including fragments, that are in orbit or re-entering the atmosphere.

s: What is the main source of space debris?
x: Fragmentation from collisions and explosions is the main source; the others are also sources of debris.

s: What did Mission Shakti, conducted on 27 March 2019, involve?
o: The deployment of India's first space station
A soft landing of a rover on the Moon
A kinetic-kill ASAT test that destroyed Microsat-R at about 300 km
A test of a reusable launch vehicle at 300 km altitude
x: Mission Shakti was a DRDO kinetic-kill anti-satellite test that destroyed the Indian satellite Microsat-R at approximately 300 km altitude, raising debris concerns.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about space debris risks?
o: Kessler Syndrome is a self-sustaining cascade of debris-creating collisions that can make orbits unusable
MMOD (micrometeoroids and orbital debris) is the top risk mainly in geostationary orbit
Kessler Syndrome is named after NASA scientist Donald Kessler
The Kessler Syndrome idea dates from 1978
x: MMOD is the top risk in low Earth orbit (LEO), not GEO.

s: In which year did Donald Kessler of NASA describe the Kessler Syndrome?
x: Kessler described the syndrome in 1978: debris density leads to collisions, more fragments and unusable orbits.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Kessler Syndrome:
1. High debris density leads to collisions.
2. Collisions produce more fragments.
3. It makes orbits more usable over time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Density leads to collisions and more fragments, which make orbits unusable, so statement 3 is wrong.

s: According to ESA (2025), the number of space objects larger than 1 cm is over:
x: ESA (2025) counts over 1.2 million objects larger than 1 cm.

s: MMOD (micrometeoroids and orbital debris) is the top risk in which orbit?
x: MMOD is the top risk in low Earth orbit, not GEO.

s: Which organisation conducted Mission Shakti, India's first anti-satellite test, in 2019?
x: Mission Shakti (27 March 2019) was a DRDO kinetic-kill ASAT test that destroyed Microsat-R.

s: Which of the following pairs about ISRO's POEM platform is correctly matched?
o: POEM drag sails – re-entry within decades instead of months
x: POEM-4 belonged to the SpaDeX/PSLV-C60 mission and fell into the Indian Ocean on 4 April 2025; its inflatable sails make it re-enter within months rather than decades.

s: On which mission did POEM-4, which re-entered over the Indian Ocean on 4 April 2025, fly?
x: POEM-4 flew on PSLV-C60 (SpaDeX); PSLV-C62 planned a PS4 de-boost.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about space-sustainability challenges facing India?
o: Space debris threatens Gaganyaan and India's in-orbit satellites
Differences in national licensing conditions may push operators to permissive regimes
Mega-constellations are a newer challenge not adequately addressed by older treaties
Existing treaties adequately address the cumulative harm caused by orbital debris
x: The treaties date from the 1960s–70s and do not adequately address cumulative debris harm or mega-constellations.

s: Which Article of the Outer Space Treaty deals with national responsibility, including for private actors?
x: Article VI deals with national responsibility; Article VII concerns liability and Article IX due regard and environmental considerations.

s: Which of the following is identified as a significant legal gap in India's space sector?
o: Absence of a national space policy
Absence of a Space Activities Act addressing liability
Absence of a body to authorise private space activities
x: India does not have a Space Activities Act specifically addressing liability, which is identified as a significant legal gap.

s: In which year did India ratify the Outer Space Treaty of 1967?
x: India is a party to the Outer Space Treaty, which bars national appropriation of space, and ratified it in 1982.

s: Which space treaty has India signed but not ratified?
x: The Moon Agreement is the only one India has signed but not ratified.

s: What is the nature of a launching State's liability under the Liability Convention, 1972, for damage caused by its space object?
o: Absolute for damage on the Earth's surface and fault-based for damage in outer space
Fault-based for damage on the Earth's surface and absolute for damage in outer space
Absolute in all cases, whether the damage is on Earth or in outer space
Limited to damage caused by private operators only
x: The Liability Convention (1972), to which India is a party, makes the launching State absolutely liable for damage on the Earth's surface and liable only for fault for damage caused in outer space. Option B reverses the two rules. Option C ignores the fault standard in space. Option D is wrong because liability rests on the launching State, including for private activity.

s: Which Article of the Outer Space Treaty deals with liability?
x: Article VII deals with liability; Article VI is national responsibility and Article IX due regard.

s: On which principle is the Moon Agreement of 1979 based?
x: The Moon Agreement treats the Moon as common heritage; India signed but has not ratified it.

s: In which year was the convention requiring space objects to be registered with the UN adopted?
x: The Registration Convention is of 1975; India is a party.

s: Which of the following principles is laid down by the Outer Space Treaty of 1967?
o: No national sovereignty over outer space
Common heritage of the Moon's resources
Absolute liability for damage on Earth
Registration of space objects with the UN
x: The Outer Space Treaty says no State can claim sovereignty over outer space; the other principles belong to the Moon Agreement, Liability and Registration Conventions.

s: Which international agreement of 1968 deals with the return of astronauts?
x: The Rescue Agreement (1968) deals with the rescue and return of astronauts; India is a party.

s: By which year does India aim to make all its space missions debris-free under its Debris Free Space Missions (DFSM) pledge?
x: The DFSM target year is 2030; India made the pledge at the 2024 IADC meeting.

s: Under India's 2026 re-entry rules, aircraft and ships must be warned at least how many days before re-entry?
x: The 2026 rules require a warning at least 45 days before re-entry, not 30.

s: With what will the servicer craft of ISRO's planned Active Debris Removal mission capture a defunct rocket body?

s: Which of the following is identified as a major gap in the international governance of orbital activities?
o: Absence of international interest in space debris
Absence of any national licensing system for satellites
Absence of an international duty-of-care standard for orbits
Absence of all collision avoidance technology
x: There is no international duty-of-care standard for orbits. Differences in licensing conditions across countries can encourage operators to choose more permissive regimes.

s: At which forum did India pledge Debris Free Space Missions (DFSM) by 2030?
x: India pledged DFSM by 2030 at the 2024 meeting of the Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee (IADC).

s: Which of the following is a proposed way forward for a safer outer space?
o: Restricting the sharing of SSA data
Ending advance notices of space activities
Wider sharing of space situational awareness data
x: More SSA data-sharing, along with advance notices and hotlines, is proposed for a safer outer space.

s: Which country declared a moratorium on destructive direct-ascent anti-satellite tests in April 2022?
x: The United States declared the moratorium on destructive direct-ascent ASAT tests in April 2022, and the issue was subsequently taken up in a UNGA resolution.

s: In which year was UNCOPUOS, of which India is a founding member, established?
x: The UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space was established in 1959, and India is a founding member.

s: In which year was the Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee (IADC), of which ISRO is a member, established?
x: IADC was established in 1993 and ISRO is a member; India made its DFSM-2030 pledge at the 2024 IADC meeting.

s: In which year did India sign the Artemis Accords?
x: India signed in 2023; the US launched the Accords in 2020 as non-binding principles, and they now have over 60 signatories.

s: What is the Prevention of an Arms Race in Outer Space (PAROS)?
o: a treaty governing aircraft warnings during re-entry
a long-running agenda item of the UN Conference on Disarmament
a private debris-removal programme led by commercial firms
a bilateral satellite-navigation agreement between India and the United States
x: PAROS is a long-running agenda item in the UN Conference on Disarmament and is backed by UN General Assembly resolutions.

s: What did Prime Minister Narendra Modi advocate at the International Space Summit in Paris on 10 September 2026?
o: national ownership of all orbital regions
competition over cooperation in outer space
x: The stated approach was 'cooperation over confrontation', with the aim of a safe, secure, peaceful and sustainable space domain anchored in international law.

s: In which year did the US launch the Artemis Accords, which India signed in 2023?
x: The US launched the non-binding Artemis Accords in 2020; India signed in 2023.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Artemis Accords:
1. They are legally binding on signatories.
2. India signed them in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Accords are non-binding, so 1 is wrong; India signed them in 2023.

s: Which post does the Secretary, Department of Defence R&D, also hold?
x: In the hierarchy, the Secretary DD R&D is also Chairman DRDO, above the Director Generals and lab directors.

s: Who is the Chairman of DRDO, as stated for February 2026?

Dr Samir V. Kamat retired on 31 May 2026 — now Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh holds additional charge as DRDO Chairman (Praveen CA-360 May 2026 magazine (src/current-affairs/praveen-ca360-2026-05-magazine.txt) p.71; octlatest daily CA 4 Nov 2026 (src/current-affairs/octlatest-daily-em-ca-2026-11-04.txt) p.3)
In February 2026 the DRDO Chairman was Dr Samir V. Kamat (since 2022); he retired on 31 May 2026 (now Rajesh Kumar Singh, additional charge).

s: In DRDO's three-level leadership structure, who make up Level II?
o: The Secretary, DDR&D, who is also Chairman of DRDO
The Defence Minister and the Secretary, DDR&D
x: Level I is the Secretary DDR&D and Chairman, Level II the two DGs, and Level III the lab directors and corporate directorates.

s: Which is DRDO's parent department under the Ministry of Defence?
o: Department of Defence Research and Development
x: DRDO works under the Department of Defence R&D, whose Secretary is also Chairman of DRDO.

s: Since which year has Dr Samir V. Kamat been Chairman of DRDO?
x:
Dr Samir V. Kamat retired on 31 May 2026 — now Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh holds additional charge as DRDO Chairman (Praveen CA-360 May 2026 magazine (src/current-affairs/praveen-ca360-2026-05-magazine.txt) p.71; octlatest daily CA 4 Nov 2026 (src/current-affairs/octlatest-daily-em-ca-2026-11-04.txt) p.3)

s:
Consider the following statements about DRDO's structure:
1. The Secretary, Department of Defence R&D is also Chairman of DRDO.
2. Lab directors report directly to the Defence Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Secretary DDR&D is Chairman; lab directors report to their cluster Director General, so 2 is wrong.

s: Dr G. Satheesh Reddy, Chairman of DRDO from 2018 to 2022, is a native of which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Dr G. Satheesh Reddy, former DRDO Chairman and Scientific Adviser to the Defence Minister, is a native of Nellore.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about DRDO?
o: It was formed by merging the TDEs, the DTDP and the Defence Science Organisation
Its headquarters, DRDO Bhawan, is in Pune
It started with 10 laboratories and now runs about 52
x: DRDO Bhawan is in New Delhi.

s: In which field does DRDO's current vision seek to empower the nation with state-of-the-art indigenous technologies?
x: DRDO's current vision is to empower the nation with state-of-the-art indigenous defence and security technologies.

s:
Consider the following statements about the mission of DRDO:
1. It includes building an indigenous technology base.
2. It aims at optimising combat effectiveness and troop well-being.
3. It is directed towards greater self-reliance and reduced import dependence.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: All three are elements of DRDO's mission, along with designing and developing sensors, weapons and platforms for the Services.

s: DRDO was formed in 1958 by merging the TDEs, the DTDP and which other body?
x: DRDO came from merging the Army's TDEs, the DTDP and the Defence Science Organisation.

s: In which year was DRDO formed?
x: DRDO was formed in 1958.

s: DRDO began with 10 laboratories; about how many laboratories does it have now?
x:
Most books / old notes: about 52 labs. Strictly (now): about 41 laboratories and 5 DYSLs (DRDO website; NextGen S&T Part 2 p.49).
"about 52 laboratories" is the pre-merger count — now about 41 laboratories and 5 DRDO Young Scientist Laboratories (drdo.gov.in/about-drdo; NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 2 (src/science-tech/nextgen-st-group2-02.pdf, OCR) p.49)
DRDO began with 10 laboratories and books long gave "about 52"; after mergers DRDO now lists about 41 laboratories plus 5 Young Scientist Labs (now ~41 + 5).

s: What does DRDO's motto 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam' mean?
o: The source of strength is science
x: DRDO's motto 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam' means the source of strength is science.

s: Which one of the following combinations contains only DRDO-designed systems identified as contributing to defence self-reliance?
o: INS Vikrant, INS Viraat, INS Khanderi and Admiral Gorshkov
Agni, Prithvi, Tejas, Pinaka and Akash
x: DRDO designed or contributed to systems including Agni, Prithvi, Tejas, Pinaka and Akash, forming part of the foundation of Aatmanirbharta in defence.

s: With which company did INMAS develop the oral anti-COVID drug 2-DG?
x: 2-DG was developed by INMAS with Dr Reddy's Laboratories.

s: What is NETRA, referred to in the context of civilian applications?
o: Mini-UAV for police and disaster management
x: NETRA or Netra V2 is a mini-UAV intended for police and disaster-management applications. It should not be confused with Netra AEW&C, the airborne early-warning aircraft.

s: Which laboratories developed DRDO's bio-toilets?
x: Bio-toilets come from DRDE Gwalior and DRL Tezpur.

s: With which company did DRDO's Pune laboratories develop the Netra mini-UAV?
x: Netra, a ~1.5 kg mini-UAV for police and disaster use, was built with IdeaForge; it is different from the Netra AEW&C.

s: For what is Amtooth, a DRDO herbal product, used?
x: Amtooth treats toothache; Lukoskin is for leucoderma and Eczit for eczema.

s: Which DRDO laboratory developed Lukoskin, a herbal product for leucoderma?
x: Lukoskin, used for leucoderma, was developed by DRDO's DIBER.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: DIA-CoEs — Premier academic institutions — Critical and futuristic defence technologies
DRDO Young Scientist Laboratories — 15 laboratories — Five futuristic areas
x: DRDO Young Scientist Labs are 5 labs in 5 futuristic areas, not 15; 15 is the number of DIA-CoEs. JCBCAT is at Jadavpur University, Kolkata and DIAT Pune is a deemed university, so those pairs are correct.

s: How many DRDO Industry Academia Centres of Excellence (DIA-CoEs) have been set up at premier institutions such as IITs and IISc?
x: DIA-CoEs are a network of 15 centres at premier institutions working on critical and futuristic defence technologies.

s: With which of the following is the Agnishodh research cell associated?
o: The Indian Army at IIT Madras
The Indian Air Force at IISc Bengaluru
The Indian Navy at IIT Delhi
x: Agnishodh is the Indian Army's research cell at IIT Madras and links Army requirements with academic research and development.

s: What kind of institution is DIAT Pune, supported by DRDO?
x: DIAT Pune is a deemed university.

s: How many DRDO Young Scientist Labs were set up in 2020?
x: There are 5 Young Scientist Labs in 5 futuristic areas; 15 is the number of DIA-CoEs.

s: At which university was the Jagadish Chandra Bose Centre for Advanced Technology (JCBCAT) set up with DRDO?
x: JCBCAT was set up at Jadavpur University, Kolkata with DRDO's help.

s: Which of the following DRDO technology cluster–laboratory pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Naval Systems and Materials – GTRE, CABS
Missiles and Strategic Systems – DRDL, RCI, ASL
x: GTRE and CABS belong to the Aeronautics cluster; Naval Systems and Materials includes NSTL, NPOL and NMRL.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Life Sciences — DIPAS, DFRL, DEBEL, INMAS, DIPR
Armaments and Combat Engineering — ARDE, HEMRL
Electronics and Communication — LRDE, DLRL, DEAL, CAIR
Combat Vehicles — LRDE, DLRL, DEAL, CAIR
x: LRDE, DLRL, DEAL and CAIR belong to the Electronics and Communication cluster. The Combat Vehicles cluster comprises CVRDE and VRDE.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the Hyderabad missile-laboratory cluster?
o: ARDE, HEMRL, NSTL, CAIR and ADE
LRDE, CVRDE, VRDE, DEAL and NPOL
DFRL, INMAS, DIPAS, DIPR and NMRL
DRDL, RCI, ASL, DMRL and DLRL
x: DRDL, RCI, ASL, DMRL and DLRL are all located in Hyderabad. They cover missile development, guidance, ballistic missiles, materials and electronic warfare.

s: DIPAS, DFRL, DEBEL and INMAS belong to which DRDO technology cluster?
x: These four labs form the Life Sciences cluster.

s: CVRDE and VRDE form which DRDO technology cluster?
x: CVRDE and VRDE make up the Combat Vehicles cluster; ARDE and HEMRL are Armaments.

s: Rustom/TAPAS BH-201, Nishant and Lakshya are associated with which DRDO laboratory?
o: Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics
x: The Aeronautical Development Establishment (ADE), Bengaluru works on UAVs such as Rustom/TAPAS BH-201, Nishant and the Lakshya target drone.

s: Personnel of which bodies are trained at the CBRN Field Training Centre under INMAS, Delhi?
x: The centre trains personnel of the Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Home Affairs and National Disaster Management Authority in CBRN preparedness.

s: Which Hyderabad DRDO laboratory works on electronic warfare?
x: DLRL is the electronic-warfare lab; DRDL develops missiles such as MPATGM, ASL handles Agni and DMRL works on metals and armour.

s: The Pinaka system was designed by which DRDO laboratory?
x: ARDE, Pune (guns, ammunition, warheads) designed Pinaka, with HEMRL, Pune as partner.

s: Where is DIPAS, the DRDO laboratory that studies soldier physiology at high altitude and in cold, located?
x: DIPAS is in Delhi; Dehradun hosts DEAL.

s: Which DRDO laboratory works on fuel-cell Air Independent Propulsion (AIP)?
x: Fuel-cell AIP is NMRL's work; NPOL, Kochi works on sonars.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about DRDO's naval laboratories?
o: NSTL works on torpedoes and mines
x: NPOL is at Kochi; the Visakhapatnam laboratory is NSTL, which works on torpedoes and mines.

s: The bike ambulance was developed by which DRDO laboratory?
x: INMAS developed the bike ambulance; DEBEL made the medical oxygen plant and DRL, Tezpur the snake repellent.

s: What is the status of the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA), which designs the LCA Tejas with DRDO?
o: An autonomous society under the Ministry of Defence
A directorate of the Indian Air Force
x: ADA is an autonomous society under the Ministry of Defence, not itself a DRDO laboratory.

s: Where is DFRL, DRDO's laboratory for food and MREs, located?
x: DFRL is at Mysuru.

s: On what does CAIR, Bengaluru work?
x: CAIR works on AI and robotics; DLRL is electronic warfare, DEBEL oxygen plants and NPOL sonars.

s: The Agni series of missiles is handled by which Hyderabad laboratory?
x: ASL handles the Agni series; DRDL develops MPATGM and RCI guidance and seekers.

s: In what does Research Centre Imarat (RCI), Hyderabad specialise?
x: RCI works on guidance and seekers; DMRL handles metals and armour.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: CVRDE, which works on the Arjun tank, is at Chennai, not Pune.

s: Which Hyderabad laboratory of DRDO works on metals, alloys and armour?
x: DMRL (Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory), Hyderabad works on metals, alloys and armour.

s: Which DRDO laboratory develops the MPATGM?
x: DRDL, Hyderabad is DRDO's missile laboratory and works on the MPATGM.

s: Which DRDO laboratory at Pune works on explosives?
x: HEMRL, Pune works on explosives; ARDE, Pune works on guns and warheads (Pinaka).

s: Which DRDO laboratory developed the Arjun tank?
x: CVRDE, Chennai is the combat-vehicle lab behind the Arjun main battle tank.

s: What is the full form of NSTL, the DRDO laboratory at Visakhapatnam?
x: NSTL = Naval Science and Technological Laboratory, Visakhapatnam; it developed the Varunastra torpedo.

s:

B. DMRL

s: DRDO's medical oxygen plant technology comes from which Bengaluru laboratory?
x: DEBEL, Bengaluru developed the medical oxygen plant.

s: Under which programme is the Technology Development Fund (TDF), a Ministry of Defence programme executed by DRDO, implemented?
x: TDF is a Ministry of Defence flagship programme executed by DRDO under the Make in India initiative.

s: What kind of access to DRDO patents has Indian industry got through Transfer of Technology since 2020?
x: Since 2020 access to DRDO patents is royalty-free; DRDO has given more than 2,100 free ToTs and opened its test facilities to the private sector.

s: Which of the following groups consists only of conventional DRDO missiles approved for technology transfer to private industry in August 2026?
x: The approved conventional-missile group comprises Astra, Rudram, Nag and VSHORADS. Nuclear-capable Agni and K-series missiles remain in state production.

s: Under DRDO's Technology Development Fund, up to what amount may the grant to industry, including MSMEs and start-ups, extend?
x: TDF grants extend up to ₹50 crore to support co-development of emerging technologies.

s: DRDO assisted ISRO in testing which system associated with the Gaganyaan programme?
x: DRDO helped ISRO test the Gaganyaan crew-escape parachute recovery system.

s: More than how many free Transfers of Technology has DRDO given to Indian industry?
x: DRDO has given 2,100+ free ToTs and opened test facilities to the private sector.

s: Under the August 2026 decision, which missiles stay in state production?
x: Astra, Rudram, Nag and VSHORADS were approved for ToT; Agni and K-series stay in state production.

s: What is DRDO's budget allocation for 2026-27?
x: DRDO got ₹29,100.25 crore in 2026-27, up from ₹26,816.82 crore in 2025-26; ₹17,250.25 crore of it is for capital spending.

s: Nagayalanka in Krishna district is associated with which of the following?
o: A CBRN training centre for national agencies
A naval weapons laboratory for underwater batteries
An aircraft integration complex for flight testing
A DRDO missile test range for flight trials of tactical missiles
x: Nagayalanka in coastal Krishna district is the site of DRDO's planned missile test range for flight trials of tactical missiles. NSTL Visakhapatnam is the naval weapons lab, the ADA flight-testing complex is in Sri Sathya Sai district, and the CBRN Field Training Centre is in Delhi.

s: Which DRDO laboratory is located at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh?
x: NSTL is at Visakhapatnam; other AP defence locations include the Kurnool test range, the planned Nagayalanka range and the ADA complex in Sri Sathya Sai district.

s: Near which place were the final trials of the ULPGM-V3 missile conducted?
x: The ULPGM-V3 final trials were done near Kurnool; Nagayalanka is a planned missile test range.

s: The ADA flight-testing complex costing ₹15,803 crore is planned in which Andhra Pradesh district?
x: The ADA flight-testing complex is planned in Sri Sathya Sai district.

s: Which of the following has NSTL, Visakhapatnam developed?
x: NSTL develops Varunastra, mines and SMART; Pinaka is ARDE's.

s: What is Agni-VI in the context of India's missile programme?
x: Agni-VI is described as a proposed longer-range intercontinental ballistic missile.

s: Which force operates India's Agni missiles, built by DRDO?
x: Agni is DRDO-built, fully indigenous and operated by the Strategic Forces Command.

s: Which of the following describes Agni-I?
o: Two-stage liquid-fuel missile of about 2,000–3,000 km range
Single-stage solid-fuel missile of about 700–800 km range
Single-stage liquid-fuel missile of about 150 km range
Three-stage solid-fuel missile of about 5,000 km range
x: Agni-I is a single-stage solid-fuel missile with a range of about 700–800 km and is approximately 15 metres long.

s: How many stages does Agni-V, a solid-fuel, canister-launched missile, have?
x: Agni-V is a three-stage solid-fuel, canister-launched missile with a stated range of 5,000 km or more; MIRV has been tested with it.

s: Which of the following pairs about the Agni series is correctly matched?
x: Agni-II is a two-stage solid-fuel missile (2,000–3,500 km). Agni-IV is two-stage and road-mobile (about 4,000 km), Agni-III has about 3,500 km range, and the three-stage canisterised missile is Agni-V.

s: From which platform was Agni-Prime test-fired on 24 September 2025?
x: Agni-Prime, a canisterised 1,000–2,000 km missile, was fired from a rail-based mobile launcher.

s: Mission Divyastra (2024) tested MIRV technology on which missile?
x: Mission Divyastra, conducted in 2024, flight-tested Agni-V with Multiple Independently targetable Re-entry Vehicles (MIRVs).

s: What is the formal ICBM range threshold that places Agni-V's 5,000 km range in the IRBM class?
x: The ICBM threshold cited is 5,500 km, so Agni-V is formally an IRBM, though some sources call it an ICBM.

s: Which Agni variant is a two-stage, road-mobile missile with a range of about 4,000 km?
x: Agni-IV is two-stage and road-mobile with about 4,000 km range; Agni-V is three-stage with 5,000+ km.

s: What is the range of Prithvi, a liquid-fuelled surface-to-surface short-range ballistic missile?
x: Prithvi is a surface-to-surface SRBM with a range of 150–350 km and uses liquid fuel.

s: At about what speed does Akash, a medium-range surface-to-air missile, travel?
x: Akash is a medium-range SAM with a range of about 25-30 km, a speed of about Mach 2.5 and an altitude capability of 18 km.

s: Which missile has a range of about 25–30 km?
x: Akash, a medium-range SAM, has a range of about 25–30 km. Trishul reaches about 9 km, Nag 500 m to 4 km (land version), and Agni about 700 km to over 5,000 km.

s: Which of the following missile names is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
x: Trishul means Trident; it is Agni that means Fire.

s:
Consider the following statements about Trishul:
1. It is a short-range, low-level quick-reaction surface-to-air missile.
2. Its range is about 9 km.
3. It was inducted into the Army.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Trishul is a short-range quick-reaction SAM of about 9 km range, but it was never inducted and was shut in 2008.

s: What is DRDO's Lakshya?
x: Lakshya is a target drone; Pinaka is a rocket launcher, Tejas an aircraft and Nishant a UAV.

s: With which country did India jointly develop BrahMos, which was not a missile of the IGMDP?
x: BrahMos was developed jointly by India and Russia; it was not part of the IGMDP.

s: HELINA is the helicopter-launched version of which missile?
x: HELINA is the helicopter-launched Nag, a fire-and-forget anti-tank missile.

s: What is meant by the term 'fire-and-forget' in missile technology?
o: The missile is incapable of changing its course after launch.
The missile can guide itself after launch, allowing the operator to take cover.
The missile is fired only after the target has been destroyed by another weapon.
The missile must remain continuously controlled by the operator until impact.
x: A fire-and-forget missile guides itself after launch, enabling the operator to seek cover or perform another task.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Nag uses an Imaging Infra-Red seeker, whereas Akash Prime uses an active RF seeker and SANT uses Lock-On After Launch. Therefore, Nag with an active RF seeker is not correctly matched.

s: What is Nag Mk-2, the tracked fire-and-forget 'tank killer' approved for Army procurement, called?
x: NAMIS is the tracked Nag Mk-2; Dhruvastra is the IAF's helicopter-launched Nag, HELINA the Army Aviation version and SANT an air-launched stand-off ATGM.

s: For which service is HELINA, the helicopter-launched variant of the Nag missile, meant?
x: HELINA is the helicopter-launched Nag variant for Army Aviation, whereas Dhruvastra is intended for the Indian Air Force.

s: Each Nag Missile Carrier (NAMICA) can carry up to how many missiles?
x: Each NAMICA, a tracked amphibious vehicle, can carry up to six Nag missiles.

s: What does an anti-tank missile generally do in the top-attack mode?
o: Approaches at ground level and hits the side armour
Climbs and then dives onto the tank's thinner top armour
Strikes the thick frontal armour head-on
Hits the tracks to immobilise the tank
x: In top attack, the missile climbs and then dives onto the tank's thinner top armour; Nag has both top-attack and direct-attack modes.

s: For which service is Dhruvastra, the helicopter-launched Nag variant, meant?
x: HELINA is the Army Aviation version, while Dhruvastra is the IAF version.

s: Which guidance mode does SANT, the air-launched stand-off anti-tank missile, use?
x: SANT (15–20 km) uses Lock-On After Launch (LOAL).

s: What is the range of the Nag-family MPATGM, a man-portable anti-tank missile?
x: MPATGM reaches about 2.5 km; NAMIS reaches 7–10 km and SANT 15–20 km.

s: The Nag anti-tank missile uses which type of seeker?
x: Nag uses an IIR seeker; Akash Prime uses an active RF seeker.

s: Which was the first missile developed under the IGMDP?
x: Prithvi was the first IGMDP missile; Prithvi-I serves the Army and Prithvi-II the Air Force.

s: Which type of fuel do Prithvi-I and Prithvi-II use?
x: Prithvi-I and Prithvi-II use liquid fuel, whereas Agni-I uses solid fuel.

s: In which year was Prithvi-II, first tested in 1996, inducted?
x: Prithvi-II was inducted in 2003; the naval version is Dhanush.

s: Which service operates Dhanush, the ship-launched version of the Prithvi missile?
x: Dhanush (Prithvi-III) is the Navy's ship-launched Prithvi; Prithvi-I is the Army's 150 km version.

s: Which service operates Prithvi-II, the variant with a range of about 350 km?
x: Prithvi-II is the Air Force version; Prithvi-I is the Army's and Dhanush the Navy's.

s: What is PAD (Pradyumna) in India's missile programme?

s: Which service operates the Prithvi-I missile?
x: Prithvi-I (150 km) is the Army version; Prithvi-II is for the Air Force and Dhanush for the Navy.

s: Which one of the following statements about Trishul is NOT correct?

It was inducted into regular service after successful development.
It is a short-range, low-level surface-to-air missile.

s: Which services use the Akash surface-to-air missile?

s: In which year was the Trishul surface-to-air missile programme shut down?
x: Trishul was never inducted; the programme was shut on 27 February 2008.

s: On which date was Akash Prime, an upgraded Akash Mk-I with an indigenous active RF seeker, first tested?

s: What is the approximate range of the canister-launched Akash-NG?
