x: The Indian Air Force was associated with Israeli Spyder, the Navy with Barak-1 and the Army with Akash.

s: Which is the later indigenous short-range successor to Trishul?
x: QRSAM, or Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile, is the later indigenous short-range successor to Trishul.

s: Which radar does Akash Mk-I use for command guidance?
x: Akash Mk-I relies on command guidance and the Rajendra radar.

s: What is Akashteer, developed by BEL with the Indian Army?
x: Akashteer is an air-defence control system, not a missile.

s: Off the coast of which state does Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, used for missile trials, lie?
x: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island is off the Odisha coast; ranges on the AP and Odisha coasts support sea-skimming trials such as LRAShM.

s: What was Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island formerly known as?
x: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island was formerly known as Wheeler Island and lies off the Odisha coast.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island — Rajasthan
Integrated Test Range, Chandipur — Andhra Pradesh
x: The Pokhran Field Firing Range is in Rajasthan. The Kurnool DRDO range is in Andhra Pradesh, while Chandipur and Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island are in Odisha.

s: As which member did India join the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR) in June 2016?
x: India entered the MTCR in June 2016 as its 35th member, which eased its BrahMos exports and high-tech imports.

s: The Kurnool DRDO missile range is located in which state?
x: The Kurnool DRDO range is in Andhra Pradesh; Chandipur and Kalam Island are in Odisha.

s: The Integrated Test Range (ITR) at Chandipur is in which district of Odisha?
x: ITR Chandipur lies in Balasore district, Odisha.

s: In May 1992, the USA put which Indian organisation on hold under the MTCR?
x: The US placed ISRO on hold under the MTCR in May 1992.

s: The Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR), which India joined in 2016, mainly controls missiles able to carry what payload over what range?
x: MTCR covers missiles that can carry 500 kg over 300 km; India joined in June 2016 as the 35th member.

s: By what name is Dr Tessy Thomas, who played a key role in Agni-V, popularly called?
x: Dr Tessy Thomas, the 'Missile Woman of India', played a key role in Agni-V and is called 'Agniputri'.

s: V.K. Saraswat is associated with which part of India's missile programme?
x: V.K. Saraswat worked on Prithvi and the Ballistic Missile Defence programme.

s: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam served as Chief Scientific Adviser at which event?
x: Kalam was CSA at Pokhran-II in 1998, not Pokhran-I.

s: Who is known as the 'Missile Man' of India?
x: APJ Abdul Kalam, who led the IGMDP, is called the 'Missile Man'; Tessy Thomas is the 'Missile Woman'.

s: APJ Abdul Kalam, leader of the IGMDP, served as which President of India?
x: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam was the 11th President of India (2002-07).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam?
o: He was project director of SLV-III
SLV-III, under his direction, launched Rohini
He was the first Indian Head of State to fly a fighter aircraft
He was Chief Scientific Adviser at the 1974 Pokhran-I test
x: Kalam was Chief Scientific Adviser at Pokhran-II in 1998, not Pokhran-I in 1974.

s: Under the IGMDP, which missile was developed during the 1992–2008 phase?
x: Prithvi and Trishul were developed in 1984–89, Nag and Akash in 1989–92, and Agni in 1992–2008.

s: Which was the nodal laboratory of the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP)?
x: DRDL, Hyderabad was the nodal lab, working with RCI and ASL; IGMDP was launched in 1983 under Kalam.

s: Under the Ministry of Defence approval, to whom is the technology of conventional missiles such as Nag transferred?
x: Conventional missiles, including Nag, go to private industry, while Agni remains in state production.

s: Which one of the following is NOT an identified spin-off of the IGMDP?
x: Long-range tracking systems, composites, ring laser gyros and radomes were identified as IGMDP spin-offs. A satellite-based navigation constellation is not included in this list.

s: Why is the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme regarded as significant?
o: Ended all missile development in India after the completion of Prithvi.
Turned India from a missile importer into a missile-exporting power and formed a base for later Agni-V MIRV, BMD and BrahMos-era programmes.
Restricted India to importing surface-to-air missiles from foreign suppliers.
Was created exclusively for developing civilian launch vehicles.
x: The IGMDP transformed India from a missile importer into a missile-exporting power and provided the foundation for Agni-V MIRV, ballistic missile defence and BrahMos-era programmes.

s: In which year was the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP) officially completed?
x: IGMDP ran from 1983 and was officially completed in 2008; later missiles became separate projects.

s: In which year was the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme launched?
x: IGMDP was launched in 1983 under Dr APJ Abdul Kalam and was officially completed in 2008.

s: Which missiles were developed in the first phase (1984-89) of the IGMDP?
x: Prithvi and Trishul came in the first phase (1984-89); Nag and Akash in 1989-92; Agni matured by 2008.

s: What is DRDO's share in BrahMos Aerospace?
x: DRDO holds 50.5% and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya 49.5%.

s: Where did BrahMos have its first successful test on 12 June 2001?
x: BrahMos, a supersonic cruise missile of about Mach 2.8–3.0, was first successfully tested at Chandipur, Odisha.

s: Which engine follows the solid booster in BrahMos?
x: BrahMos has a solid booster and a liquid ramjet, combines inertial and satellite navigation, and is canister-launched in fire-and-forget mode.

s: Which BrahMos variant is a planned hypersonic missile capable of speeds above Mach 5?
x: BrahMos-II is the planned hypersonic variant; BrahMos-NG is a lighter version for platforms such as Tejas.

s: During which operation was BrahMos reportedly used in combat for the first time?
x: The first reported combat use of BrahMos was during Operation Sindoor in May 2025.

s: Where is the BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility, inaugurated on 11 May 2025, located?
x: The BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility at Lucknow (in the UP defence corridor) was inaugurated on 11 May 2025, with the first batch flagged off within five months. Hyderabad and Nagpur are other defence-industry centres, and Chandipur is the test range where BrahMos was first tested in 2001.

s: Where was the Inter-Governmental Agreement that created BrahMos Aerospace signed in 1998?
x: The India-Russia IGA was signed in Moscow in 1998 and created BrahMos Aerospace.

s: Which BrahMos variant is lighter (about 1.5 t) and meant for Tejas, smaller warships and submarines?
x: BrahMos-NG weighs about 1.5 t against 2.5 t of the base missile; BrahMos-II is the planned hypersonic one.

s: From the names of which two rivers is the name 'BrahMos' derived?
x: BrahMos joins the Brahmaputra of India and the Moskva of Russia, the two partner countries.

s: BrahMos Aerospace is a joint venture of DRDO and which Russian company?
x: BrahMos Aerospace is owned by DRDO (50.5%) and NPO Mashinostroyeniya (NPOM) of Russia (49.5%).

s: What type of missile is BrahMos?
x: BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile flying at Mach 2.8–3.0.

s: After India joined which regime in 2016 was the range of BrahMos raised beyond 290 km?
x: MTCR limits missile exports above 300 km; after India joined MTCR in 2016 BrahMos range was raised towards about 450 km.

s: From which moving warship was BrahMos fired on 21 March 2010 off the Odisha coast?
x: On 21 March 2010 BrahMos was fired from the moving warship INS Ranvir in the Bay of Bengal.

s: What is the speed of the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile?
x: BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile flying at Mach 2.8–3.0 (about 3,400–3,700 km/h).

s: From which fighter aircraft is the air-launched BrahMos fired?
x: BrahMos can be launched from land, ship, submarine and air; its air platform is the Su-30MKI.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's missile exports?
o: The Philippines is India's first BrahMos export customer
BrahMos deliveries to the Philippines began in 2024
BrahMos and Akashteer have already been delivered to the UAE
The Astra Mk-1 deal with Indonesia (July 2026) is the first Astra-family export
x: With the UAE, BrahMos and Akashteer talks are only at an early stage; nothing has been delivered.

s: Which country was the first export customer of BrahMos?
x: The Philippines signed a $375 million deal (January 2022) for three batteries; the first batch was delivered in April 2024.

s: In which year did the Philippines sign the $375 million deal to buy shore-based BrahMos missiles from India?
x: The Philippines signed the $375 million BrahMos deal in January 2022; the first batch was delivered in April 2024.

s: How many batteries of shore-based anti-ship BrahMos does the Philippines deal of January 2022 cover?
x: The $375 million deal is for three batteries of shore-based anti-ship BrahMos.

s: Which of the following describes the Minuteman III?
o: An American ICBM forming the land leg of the US nuclear triad
x: Minuteman III is a United States intercontinental ballistic missile and forms the land leg of the US nuclear triad.

s: Which is Russia's ship-launched hypersonic missile?
x: Zircon is ship-launched; Kinzhal is air-launched. Hwasong is North Korean and Fattah Iranian.

s: Which one of the following groups contains only missiles associated with Russia?
x: BrahMos is a joint venture with Russia, while R-73 Archer and S-400 are Russian systems. The other groups contain missiles associated with Israel, Iran, North Korea, Pakistan or the United States.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Spyder is an Israeli system used by the Indian Air Force and replaced Trishul. Iran is associated with Shahab and Fattah, not Spyder.

s: Which of the following pairs of missile and country is correctly matched?
x: Hwasong is North Korea's; Shahab and Fattah are Iran's and Abdali is Pakistan's.

s: From which platform is Kinzhal, Russia's hypersonic missile, launched?
x: Kinzhal is air-launched; Zircon is Russia's ship-launched hypersonic cruise missile.

s: What does the word 'Barak' in Barak-8, a missile developed with Israel, mean?
x: 'Barak' means Lightning in Hebrew; Barak-8/MRSAM is a DRDO–IAI medium-range SAM.

s: On which ship was the Barak-1 missile system first deployed in the Indian Navy?
x: Barak-1, bought from Israel for the Navy, was first deployed on the aircraft carrier INS Virat.

s: Which engine powers Nirbhay, India's subsonic long-range land-attack cruise missile?
x: Nirbhay is turbojet-powered; the liquid ramjet belongs to the supersonic BrahMos.

s: Which propulsion system powers Astra Mk-3 'Gandiva'?
x: Gandiva uses an SFDR with range of 350+ km; the dual-pulse solid motor powers Astra Mk-2.

s: Which engine powers the Indigenous Technology Cruise Missile (ITCM), successor to Nirbhay?
x: ITCM is the successor to Nirbhay and is powered by the indigenous Manik small turbofan engine developed by GTRE.

s: What is the range of Astra Mk-1, carried on the Su-30MKI?
x: Astra Mk-1 reaches 80–110 km; Mk-2 about 200 km and Mk-3 'Gandiva' 350+ km.

s: What is the range of Nirbhay, India's subsonic long-range land-attack cruise missile?
x: Nirbhay is a turbojet-powered subsonic cruise missile with a range of about 1,000 km.

s: To which family of missiles does Astra, developed by DRDO with an active radar seeker, belong?
x: Astra is a DRDO-developed family of beyond-visual-range air-to-air missiles using an active radar seeker.

s: Which country signed the deal for the first-ever export of the Astra Mk-1 missile (July 2026)?
x: Indonesia's July 2026 deal is the first-ever Astra export; the Philippines bought BrahMos.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: MPATGM — Third-generation fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile
Prahaar — About 150 km tactical ballistic missile
VSHORADS — Man-portable air-defence system against low-altitude threats
x: LRGB Gaurav is a 1,000 kg glide bomb with a range of about 100 km, released from the Su-30MKI. The 120 km guided rocket is Pinaka LRGR-120.

s: Which is India's first indigenous anti-radiation missile, designed to home passively on radar emissions?
x: Rudram-I is India's first indigenous anti-radiation missile. It passively homes on radar emissions to destroy enemy radars and communication sites.

s: Which one of the following missiles is a canister-launched, hypersonic, nuclear-capable surface-to-surface tactical missile with a range of about 700–1,900 km?
x: Shaurya is a canister-launched hypersonic surface-to-surface tactical missile with a range of about 700–1,900 km and nuclear capability.

s: What is the stated range of Pralay, a quasi-ballistic short-range surface-to-surface missile?
x: Pralay has a 150–500 km range, a conventional warhead and manoeuvrable re-entry capability.

s: From which missile is VL-SRSAM, the vertical-launch short-range SAM for Navy ships, derived?
x: VL-SRSAM is derived from the Astra air-to-air missile.

s: Which missile forms the Army's mid-range layer of the integrated air defence weapon system against low-flying threats?
x: QRSAM (Quick Reaction SAM) is the Army's mid-range IADWS layer; VSHORADS is man-portable.

s: Which is India's first indigenous helicopter-launched anti-ship missile?
x: NASM-SR (Naval Anti-Ship Missile – Short Range) is the first indigenous helicopter-launched anti-ship missile, with an IIR seeker.

s: Which DRDO laboratory developed the canister-launched Shaurya missile?
o: Combat Vehicles Research and Development Establishment (CVRDE)
x: Shaurya, a canister-launched hypersonic surface-to-surface missile, was developed by DRDO's ASL, Hyderabad.

s: In which city is the Advanced Systems Laboratory (ASL) of DRDO, which developed the Shaurya missile, located?
x: ASL, the DRDO lab that developed Shaurya, is in Hyderabad.

s: When was Mission Shakti, the joint DRDO–ISRO anti-satellite test, conducted?
x: It was conducted on 27 March 2019; Microsat-R was hit in low LEO (~283 km) so the debris would decay quickly.

s: In Mission Shakti, the live satellite Microsat-R was destroyed by which DRDO interceptor?
x: A DRDO PDV Mk-II interceptor destroyed the live satellite Microsat-R during Mission Shakti.

s: India became the fourth country to demonstrate an anti-satellite capability. Which of the following shows the three countries that preceded India?
x: India became the fourth country with demonstrated ASAT capability after the USA, Russia and China.

s: At what altitude in Low Earth Orbit was the target satellite destroyed in Mission Shakti?
x: Microsat-R was hit at about 283 km in low LEO, chosen so that debris decays quickly.

s: Which launch vehicle put Microsat-R, the target of Mission Shakti, into orbit in January 2019?
x: Microsat-R, a DRDO satellite, was launched by PSLV-C44 in January 2019.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Mission Shakti?
o: It was done in the upper atmosphere to ensure no debris
It used the DRDO PDV Mk-II interceptor
It was a joint DRDO–ISRO effort
It destroyed a live satellite in Low Earth Orbit
x: The test was in low LEO (~283 km) so debris would decay quickly; 'upper atmosphere, no debris' is wrong.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Mission Shakti – Made India the third country to demonstrate an ASAT capability
x: Mission Shakti made India the fourth country, not the third, to demonstrate an ASAT capability.

s: Which type of missile stays powered throughout its flight and uses aerodynamic lift at relatively low altitude?
x: A cruise missile is powered throughout; a ballistic missile is powered mainly in boost phase and then follows a high parabolic arc.

s: Which of the following characterises a scramjet engine?
o: Subsonic combustion after the air is slowed down
Supersonic combustion and no rotating parts
Carrying all the oxygen needed for combustion
x: A scramjet uses supersonic combustion and has no rotating compressor or turbine parts; unlike a rocket, it does not carry its oxidiser.

s: For which of the following is Solid Fuel Ducted Ramjet (SFDR) technology mainly intended?
x: SFDR uses atmospheric air for combustion and was demonstrated from ITR Chandipur for application in long-range air-to-air missiles.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about MIRV and Mission Divyastra?
o: Mission Divyastra used the K-4 missile
Mission Divyastra used the Agni-V missile
A MIRV lets one missile carry several warheads aimed at different targets
Mission Divyastra was India's first MIRV flight test
x: Mission Divyastra used Agni-V, not K-4; K-4 is a submarine-launched missile.

s: Which of the following Indian missiles is subsonic?
x: Nirbhay is subsonic; BrahMos is supersonic and BrahMos-II is hypersonic.

s: What is a vehicle that is rocket-boosted, then glides at Mach 5+ and manoeuvres in the upper atmosphere called?
x: An HGV glides at Mach 5+ after a rocket boost and is hard to intercept.

s: On which date was the first flight-trial of India's long-range hypersonic missile reported?
x: India's first reported flight-trial of the long-range hypersonic missile took place on 16 November 2024.

s: Above which speed is a missile called hypersonic?
x: Hypersonic means faster than Mach 5; a Hypersonic Glide Vehicle glides at Mach 5+ while manoeuvring.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's HSTDV:
1. It flew at above Mach 6.
2. It validated scramjet combustion and thermal protection above 2,000°C.
3. It is a submarine-launched missile with a range of 3,500 km.
Which of the above statements are correct?
x: HSTDV flew at above Mach 6 and validated scramjet combustion and thermal protection above 2,000°C; it is not a submarine-launched missile.

s: What is the peak speed of India's long-range hypersonic anti-ship missile, which uses skipping manoeuvres?
x: It reportedly peaks at about Mach 10, with an average speed of about Mach 5.

s: For which purpose were the ranges along the Andhra Pradesh coast used in January 2026?
o: Testing of the Astra export configuration
Demonstration of the first indigenous anti-radiation missile
x: Ranges along the Andhra Pradesh coast were used for LRAShM validation rounds.

s: What is the approximate range of LR-AShM, India's hypersonic glide anti-ship missile for Navy coastal batteries?
x: LR-AShM has a range of about 1,500 km, with a peak speed of Mach 10.

s: Pokhran-II was conducted under which Prime Minister?
x: Pokhran-II was conducted under A.B. Vajpayee, with A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and R. Chidambaram in the scientific leadership.

s: Who led the team that conducted Pokhran-I (1974)?
x: Raja Ramanna led the Pokhran-I team; Kalam and Chidambaram led Pokhran-II.

s: How many nuclear tests did India conduct in Pokhran-II (1998)?
x: Pokhran-II on 11 and 13 May 1998 had five tests, both fission and fusion.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Operation Shakti was the 1998 nuclear test; Mission Shakti was the 2019 anti-satellite test.

s: What was the code name of Pokhran-II (1998)?
x: Pokhran-II (11 and 13 May 1998) was 'Operation Shakti'; Pokhran-I (1974) was 'Smiling Buddha'.

s: Which day is observed in India on 11 May?
x: 11 May is observed as National Technology Day in India, commemorating the 1998 Pokhran tests.

s: When was India's first nuclear test, 'Smiling Buddha', conducted at Pokhran?
x: Pokhran-I, code-named Smiling Buddha, was conducted on 18 May 1974 under PM Indira Gandhi.

s: Who among the following led the Pokhran-II tests of 1998 along with R. Chidambaram of DAE?
x: Pokhran-II (Operation Shakti) was led by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam of DRDO and R. Chidambaram of DAE.

s: In which district of Rajasthan is the Pokhran Test Range located?
x: The Pokhran Test Range, site of Pokhran-I and II, is in Jaisalmer district, Rajasthan.

s: From which submarine was the K-4 SLBM first launched on 27 November 2024?
x: K-4 was first fired from INS Arighaat in the Bay of Bengal on 27 November 2024.

s: Where was INS Aridhaman, India's third SSBN, commissioned on 3 April 2026?
x: INS Aridhaman was commissioned at Visakhapatnam on 3 April 2026.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's submarine-launched missiles:
1. K-15 Sagarika has a range of about 750 km.
2. K-4 has a range of about 3,500 km.
3. INS Arighaat was India's first indigenous SSBN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: K-15 reaches about 750 km and K-4 about 3,500 km; the first indigenous SSBN was INS Arihant (2016), not Arighaat.

s: What is the range of the K-15 Sagarika submarine-launched ballistic missile?
x: K-15 Sagarika has a range of about 750 km; 3,500 km is K-4.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's SSBNs?
o: INS Aridhaman can carry 24 K-15 or 8 K-4/K-5 missiles
INS Arighaat has 8 vertical launch tubes
INS Arihant has 4 vertical launch tubes
INS Aridhaman has 8 vertical launch tubes
x: Arihant and Arighaat have 4 vertical launch tubes each; only Aridhaman has 8, which gives it the larger load.

s: What was the Advanced Technology Vessel (ATV) project undertaken to build?
x: The ATV project was initiated by DRDO and private firms, with Russian assistance, to build SSBNs.

s: Which type of submarine was INS Chakra II, leased by India from Russia?
x: INS Chakra II was a leased Akula-class SSN (formerly Nerpa); the first INS Chakra was a Charlie-class boat.

s: Which type of submarine was INS Chakra, leased from the Soviet Union in 1988?
x: INS Chakra (1988) was a Charlie-class SSN; INS Chakra II was an Akula-class SSN.

s: With help from which country did DRDO and private firms carry out the ATV project to build India's SSBNs?
x: The ATV project had Russian help.

s: Which was India's first indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN)?
x: INS Arihant, commissioned in 2016 under the ATV project, is India's first indigenous SSBN.

s: INS Shishumar and INS Shalki are diesel-electric submarines of which type?
x: INS Shalki and INS Shishumar are German-designed Type 209 diesel-electric submarines.

s: In which year was INS Chakra II, a leased Russian Akula-class nuclear attack submarine, commissioned?
x: INS Chakra II (formerly Nerpa) was commissioned on 4 April 2012.

s:
Consider the following statements about Project Kusha:
1. Its M3 interceptor is expected to reach about 350–400 km.
2. It is DRDO's short-range air-defence system.
3. Its M1 interceptor has a range of about 150 km.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Project Kusha is DRDO's long-range (not short-range) air-defence system, with M1/M2/M3 interceptors of about 150/250/350–400 km.

s: Which is the exo-atmospheric interceptor in Phase-I of India's Ballistic Missile Defence programme?
x: Phase-I uses PAD/Pradyumna (exo) and AAD/Ashwin (endo); AD-1 and AD-2 belong to Phase-II.

s: By which year does Mission Sudarshan Chakra, a multi-layered air and missile defence network, aim at operational maturity?
x: Mission Sudarshan Chakra targets operational maturity by 2035.

s: What is PAD (Prithvi Air Defence) in India's BMD programme?
x: PAD is the higher-altitude exo-atmospheric interceptor; AAD is the lower-altitude endo-atmospheric interceptor and Swordfish is a tracking radar.

s: AD-1 and AD-2 interceptors belong to which phase of India's BMD programme?
x: AD-1 and AD-2 are Phase II BMD interceptors meant for longer-range threats of about the 5,000-km class.

s: For what is the Swordfish radar primarily used?
o: Jam drone-control signals at short range
Track ballistic missiles and space objects at distances exceeding 1,500 km
x: The Long-Range Tracking Radar, known as Swordfish, tracks ballistic missiles and space objects at distances of more than 1,500 km.

s: To which phase and layer does the AAD (Advanced Air Defence) interceptor belong in India's BMD programme?
x: AAD is the Phase-I endo-atmospheric (lower altitude) interceptor; PAD is the exo-atmospheric one.

s: Which of the following jointly developed MRSAM or Barak-8?
x: MRSAM/Barak-8 is an India-Israel programme involving DRDO and Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI).

s: What is the vision year of Mission Sudarshan Chakra, a networked national shield of air defence, cybersecurity and surveillance?
x: It is Vision 2035, built from blocks such as Akash Tarang, MRSAM and VSHORADS, with Project Kusha as a core element.

s: What is Akashteer?
o: A long-range missile developed by DRDO
An automated air-defence control network built by BEL with the Army
x: Akashteer is BEL's automated air-defence control network for the Army; Akash Tarang is the anti-drone soft-kill EW system.

s:
Consider the following statements about the S-400 Triumf:
1. The Indian Air Force refers to it as 'Sudarshan Chakra'.
2. Belarus was its first foreign buyer after Russia.
3. China was its first foreign buyer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The IAF calls its S-400 'Sudarshan Chakra', and China was the first foreign buyer; Belarus came later.

s: What are the approximate interceptor ranges of Project Kusha, DRDO's long-range air-defence project?
x: Project Kusha is reported as a long-range air-defence project with M1, M2 and M3 interceptors of about 150, 250 and 350–400 km ranges, respectively.

s: India's IADWS, first tested in August 2025, combines QRSAM and VSHORADS with which of the following?
x: IADWS = QRSAM + VSHORADS + a high-power laser DEW, all indigenous.

s: What is Akash Tarang, a building block of Mission Sudarshan Chakra?
x: Akash Tarang is an indigenous anti-drone soft-kill EW system; Akashteer is the control network.

s: Which country developed the S-400 Triumf air defence system?
x: The S-400 Triumf is a Russian long-range surface-to-air missile system; the IAF calls it 'Sudarshan Chakra'.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's nuclear doctrine?
o: No First Use was first declared by the Indira Gandhi government after Pokhran-I
The draft doctrine with No First Use came from the Vajpayee government in 1999
The draft followed the Pokhran-II tests of 1998
The Cabinet Committee on Security formally adopted it on 4 January 2003
x: NFU dates from the Vajpayee government after Pokhran-II (1998), not from Pokhran-I (1974).

s: Which of the following is NOT a tenet of India's nuclear doctrine?
o: Use of nuclear weapons against every non-nuclear-weapon state
x: The doctrine provides for no use against non-nuclear-weapon states (subject to the clause on major biological or chemical attacks).

s: Against a major attack involving which weapons does India's nuclear doctrine retain the nuclear option?
x: The doctrine retains the nuclear option against a major biological or chemical attack.

s: Under India's No First Use policy, against which of the following may nuclear weapons be used in retaliation?
o: any conventional attack on Indian territory
a nuclear attack on Indian territory or Indian forces
a cyberattack on India’s strategic infrastructure
any military alliance formed against India
x: India’s No First Use policy permits nuclear weapons only in retaliation against a nuclear attack on Indian territory or Indian forces.

s: What is the Strategic Forces Command?
o: a joint research body of DRDO and ISRO
a civilian body regulating nuclear exports
a tri-service command managing and operating India’s nuclear arsenal
a parliamentary committee supervising defence expenditure
x: The Strategic Forces Command is a tri-service command responsible for managing and operating India’s nuclear arsenal.

s: Which of the following pairs about India's nuclear command structure is wrongly matched?
o: Political Council of the NCA – Headed by the Prime Minister
Executive Council of the NCA – Headed by the National Security Adviser
Cabinet Committee on Security – Manages nuclear forces
Strategic Forces Command – Manages nuclear forces
x: The Strategic Forces Command manages nuclear forces; the CCS supervises civilian political control.

s: Which body prepared India's draft nuclear doctrine of August 1999?
x: The NSAB prepared the draft in August 1999; the CCS adopted the doctrine on 4 January 2003.

s: Under India's Nuclear Command Authority, which is the only body that can authorise the use of nuclear weapons?
x: The Political Council, chaired by the PM, alone authorises use; the SFC operates the arsenal and the CCS only oversees.

s: Who chairs the Executive Council of India's Nuclear Command Authority?
x: The NSA chairs the Executive Council; the PM chairs the Political Council.

s: After which event did India's No First Use nuclear policy come from the Vajpayee government?
x: NFU was announced after Pokhran-II by the Vajpayee government, not after Pokhran-I.

s: In which year was India's tri-service Strategic Forces Command set up?
x: The Strategic Forces Command, which manages and operates the nuclear arsenal, was set up in 2003.

s: In which year did India become a member of the Wassenaar Arrangement?
x: India joined Wassenaar in 2017; it joined the MTCR and the Hague Code of Conduct in 2016 and the Australia Group in 2018.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India and nuclear regimes?
o: India has not signed the NPT, calling it discriminatory
India has been an NSG member since its 2008 waiver
India will not sign the CTBT until it is tied to time-bound global disarmament
India keeps a voluntary nuclear-test moratorium
x: India is not an NSG member (blocked by China); it got the 2008 NSG waiver and follows NSG guidelines.

s: On which condition does India support a universal and verifiable Fissile Material Cut-off Treaty?
o: does not cap India’s existing stockpile
x: India supports a universal and verifiable FMCT, but its position is that the treaty should not cap its existing stockpile.

s: Besides the WMD Act, through which list does India follow the guidelines of the NSG, MTCR, Wassenaar Arrangement and Australia Group?
